title: iMuninn unified coordinate frames
notes: The wire protocol stays in Apple / Android native frames. Clients convert once, at their entry point, with the constants below.
Every entry carries verified: false until it has been checked on a real phone (docs/dev/11-frame-convention.md section 5).
Matrices: columns are the child frame's axes expressed in the parent frame, so a_rot_b @ p_b = p_a.
Lengths in metres in this file. iphone-frames.json keeps millimetres to match the drawings.

naming.a_tf_b: 4x4 homogeneous pose of frame b in frame a: p_a = a_tf_b @ p_b
naming.a_pos_b: origin of b expressed in a (translation part of a_tf_b)
naming.a_quat_b: a_rot_b as a quaternion, (x, y, z, w)

world.definition: Origin where the AR session started. z up (against gravity), x = the camera's horizontal viewing direction at session start, y = left (FLU, REP 103). Converted from the ARKit world frame.

device.definition: Centre of the display active area, on the outer surface of the front cover glass. Core Motion axes: x right edge, y top edge, z out of the screen (portrait). Same as the iphone-frames dataset's body frame.

imu.definition: Same axes as device; origin assumed at the device origin (Apple does not publish the IMU location). See imu.lever_arm.

magsafe.definition: Centre of the MagSafe keep-out circle on the back plate; z out of the back, y = device y.

cam_main_optical.definition: Main (wide) camera. OpenCV optical axes of the unrotated native image: x right, y down, z viewing direction. Origin on the lens window, outer surface of the camera cover glass.

cam_ultra_wide_optical.definition: Ultra-wide camera, same convention as cam_main_optical.

cam_telephoto_optical.definition: Telephoto camera, same convention as cam_main_optical.

cam_front_optical.definition: Front camera. OpenCV optical axes of the unmirrored native image; z out of the screen. x / y depend on the sensor rotation (rotation_deg).

arcam.definition: ARKit camera frame (ARCamera.transform's local frame): x along the long edge toward the bottom, y up in landscape-right, z toward the screen side; the camera looks along -z. Only used to convert ARKit poses.

ar_world.definition: ARKit world frame with worldAlignment .gravity: y up, -z = camera heading at session start.

world_rot_ar.basis: derived: x_w = -z_ar, y_w = -x_ar, z_w = y_ar (ARKit .gravity world, official docs)

device_rot_arcam.basis: derived from the ARKit camera axes (official docs) and the Core Motion device axes

arcam_rot_optical.basis: Apple sample code: intrinsics frame = ARKit camera frame with y and z flipped

device_rot_rear_optical.basis: device_rot_arcam @ arcam_rot_optical; matches rotation_deg 90 (measured on iPhone 17 Pro)

device_rot_front_optical.basis: derived for rotation_deg 90 (iPhone 17 Pro, measured rotation) and an unmirrored buffer; other models use the rule in camera_optical

camera_optical.rule: native image = upright portrait image rotated counter-clockwise by rotation_deg. With (xu, yu, z) the upright axes below: 0 -> (xu, yu), 90 -> (yu, -xu), 180 -> (-xu, -yu), 270 -> (-yu, xu). A mirrored buffer is flipped back (u -> W - 1 - u, cx -> W - cx) before this applies.

ar_tracking_camera.basis: ARKit world tracking uses the main (wide) camera; DeviceInfo.ar_capture_device_type overrides it when present

ios.input: ImuSample.accel: m/s^2 with the Core Motion sign (gravity vector; flat face up z = -9.81)

android.input: ImuSample.accel: m/s^2 SensorManager sign (specific force; flat face up z = +9.81)

accel.output: specific force in m/s^2, REP 145: flat face up z = +9.81

gyro.output: rad/s about the device axes, right-handed

lever_arm.basis: IMU position not published by Apple; device origin assumed

timestamps.clock: device monotonic clock (mach_absolute_time / CLOCK_BOOTTIME), shared by every stream
